blocks.content: Igneous rocks are called primary rocks because they were the first to form during the evolution of the Earth's crust.

items: Granite and Gabbro are classic examples of Intrusive (Plutonic) rocks, whereas Basalt and Obsidian are Extrusive (Volcanic) rocks.
The Deccan Traps of India are composed primarily of extrusive basaltic lava flows.
Magma viscosity depends on silica content: Acidic magma is highly viscous and explosive, while basic magma is fluid and spreads widely.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Igneous rocks are primary rocks formed by the cooling, solidification, and crystallization of molten magma or lava.
Intrusive (Plutonic) igneous rocks cool slowly beneath the Earth's crust, developing large mineral grains.
Extrusive (Volcanic) igneous rocks cool rapidly on the Earth's surface, forming fine-grained or glassy textures.
Acidic igneous rocks contain high silica content (>65%), making them lighter in color and less dense.
Basic igneous rocks have lower silica content (45–55%) and are rich in iron and magnesium, making them dense and dark.
